data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
Key points:
  • Major development in two-year takeover battle
  • Merged bank's German headquarters to remain in Frankfurt as listed entity
  • Germany drops demand to name two Commerzbank supervisory board members
  • UniCredit pledges to add German nationals to its board of directors
  • Commerzbank welcomes agreement

By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached a deal on the main sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, marking a major breakthrough in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, set out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the minister, would keep UniCredit's enlarged German business headquartered and listed in Frankfurt, meeting a key German demand.

But in a concession to UniCredit, Germany has dropped its insistence on appointing two members to Commerzbank's supervisory board.

"I would like to thank Minister Klingbeil for his collaborative approach, which has been instrumental in bringing us to this positive outcome," Orcel said in a statement.

The veteran investment banker also welcomed Klingbeil's "endorsement" of the strategy he has mapped out for Commerzbank.

A merger of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.4 trillion) of assets spanning two of the euro zone's ​largest economies, in one of Europe's most significant cross-border banking deals in years.

The European Central Bank has long encouraged tie-ups to create larger European lenders able to compete with U.S. giants, while criticising political opposition that has stymied mergers.

Orcel said on Tuesday that UniCredit was uniquely positioned to pursue the deal because of its existing presence in Germany.

In the November 18 letter, seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles.

UniCredit also pledged to appoint German nationals to its board of directors. The bank had a German chairman for years after acquiring Bavarian bank HVB in 2005.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control".

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council," he said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

GERMAN GOVERNMENT STAKE

Commerzbank said it welcomed UniCredit's commitments and that its management would "work together with UniCredit to develop a strategy that builds on the strengths of both banks".

Commerzbank shares were up 1.8% at 0834 GMT, while UniCredit shares were up 2.4%.

The agreement clears the way for a series of steps, including UniCredit formally taking control, consolidating Commerzbank on its balance sheet and nominating supervisory board members who could appoint a new management team.

Orcel launched his pursuit of Commerzbank in 2024, catching both the lender and Berlin off guard by quietly building a stake before buying the one being sold by the state.

Commerzbank and the German government resisted the approach, ​but relented after UniCredit amassed a holding close to ​50%.

Commerzbank employees have long opposed a deal, partly because of Orcel's stated plans to cut jobs in Germany.

A key workforce representative said on Thursday he welcomed the commitment to Frankfurt remaining the German headquarters but stressed that existing labour agreements remained in force.

"If those agreements are respected as announced, there may not be years of confrontation ahead," said Sascha Uebel, head of Commerzbank's works council.

"Ultimately, it is now in Andrea Orcel's hands how we, as employees, will receive him here," he told Reuters.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

The future of that stake remains an open question. Orcel's letter said the agreement "set the basis for the disposal of the government's stake", but Klingbeil's statement contained no commitment to sell.

Klingbeil ​and Orcel met in September to discuss UniCredit's hostile €45 billion approach. Both called the talks "constructive" but differences remained.

Since then, the ECB, the European Commission and the US Federal Reserve have approved the deal.

Earlier this month, Commerzbank said it was "convinced" a tie-up with UniCredit could create value, signalling a markedly more positive stance towards a deal it had long opposed.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: South Korea's Supreme Court orders retrial for ex-PM Han over his role in martial law attempt
data.description:
By Heejin Kim and Joyce Lee

South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence for his role in the brief imposition of martial law two years ago, sending the case back to a lower court.

Former President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law in December 2024, saying it was needed to root out "anti-state forces" and overcome political deadlock. Although it only lasted about six hours, the attempt sent shockwaves through a country long viewed as one of Asia's most resilient democracies.

In making their ruling, a majority of Supreme Court justices disagreed with the appellate court's finding that Han, 77, had arranged a cabinet meeting for Yoon, intending to give legitimacy to the declaration of martial law.

The Supreme Court, however, did agree with the appellate court's finding that after martial law was declared, Han showed intent to "subvert constitutional order", citing actions such as the seeking of cabinet members' signatures on related documents.

The special prosecution team for Han's case said in a statement that they respect the court's ruling.

Han has denied wrongdoing in relation to all charges except one for perjury. He said last year that while he regretted not being able to stop Yoon from declaring martial law, he "never agreed to it ⁠or tried ​to help."

Yoon, who has denied wrongdoing, saying he exercised his powers as president, was convicted of insurrection in February and sentenced to life in prison.

He has appealed and awaits that ruling, which is scheduled for January.

In a separate case on Thursday, the Supreme Court upheld a four-year jail term for Kim Keon Hee, Yoon's wife.

She has been in prison since August 2025, convicted of stock trading manipulation and accepting bribes, including two Chanel bags from South Korea's Unification Church.

Yoon was ousted as president in April 2025 when the Constitutional Court upheld his impeachment. Two months later, his People Power Party lost the presidential election to the opposition Democratic Party's Lee Jae Myung.

data.title: Sugar maker Tereos cuts profit outlook as dire harvest weighs
data.description:
French sugar group Tereos on Thursday posted a net loss for the first half of 2026/27 and revised its core profit guidance for the full year to take account of an exceptionally poor sugar beet crop in France.

  • Record temperatures and drought in France this summer severely hurt sugar beets, pushing the harvest to its lowest level since at least 1980

  • Tereos cut its guidance for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation to between €220 million and €275 million ($241 million to $302 million) for the full 2026/27 financial year

  • That compared with a previous EBITDA target of €275 million to €350 million

  • A fall in sugar and starch prices and high energy costs weighed on sales, which fell 9% year on year to €2.34 billion in the six months to September 30, Tereos said

  • EBITDA fell 11% to €154 million over the same period. The group posted a net loss of €118 million, though narrowing from a €572 million loss a year earlier

  • The group, the world’s second-largest sugar maker because of its large operations in Brazil, maintained its full-year guidance for debt, expected at between €2.2 billion and €2.4 billion

  • It stood at €2.15 billion as of September 30, down €110 million compared to March 31 but above the €2.11 billion posted a year earlier

data.title: Equitas Small Finance Bank working to break down silo approach to building assets, liabilities: Interim Chief Balaji
data.description:
Equitas Small Finance Bank is working to break down the current silo approach to building assets and liabilities and transform into an integrated bank serving multiple needs of the same customer, said Balaji Nuthalapadi, Interim MD & CEO.

In an interaction with businessline, he emphasised that the Chennai-headquartered Bank has been able to take the recent resignation of its Founder-MD & CEO PN Vasudevan in its stride, with business continuing as usual, due to the strong leadership team that the Founder assiduously built over the years.

Nuthalapadi outlined the Bank’s plans for applying for a universal bank license within calendar year 2027, introducing new two-wheeler financing, stepping up gold loans, improving the proportion of low cost current account, savings account (CASA) deposits and reducing the cost-to-income ratio.

Edited excerpts:

Following the unexpected resignation of the MD and CEO, how is the bank managing the leadership transition? Has the development affected business momentum?

The developments of the last couple of weeks were unexpected. Mr. Vasudevan was the Founder-CEO and was synonymous with Equitas in many ways. However, the leadership team he has built is very strong. Our management team comprises 14 members, nine of whom have been associated with Equitas for several years, while five have joined relatively recently, bringing fresh perspectives.

There is a good balance of experienced professionals and new talent. For instance, our CFO joined five months ago, our Head of Internal Audit joined a little over a year ago, and I joined about 20 months ago. This strong management structure has helped ensure continuity. Immediately after the resignation, we were able to regroup and continue business as usual. Business momentum remains unaffected.

Having been with Equitas for 20 months, I am already well integrated into the bank’s governance processes and management structure. Consequently, taking over the interim responsibility for three months has been relatively seamless. Our immediate priorities are: ensuring stability and continuity; maintaining the growth momentum of the last few quarters; achieving our loan disbursement targets; and delivering on the full-year business plan.

We disbursed approximately ₹7,450 crore last quarter and expect to exceed that figure in the current quarter. Our focus is also on sustaining the momentum into Q4.

Your bank’s cost-to-income (CI) ratio is relatively high at about 69%. How do you plan to bring it down, and what is your target?

Reducing the CI ratio is one of our key priorities. We believe the biggest opportunity lies in improving cross-selling and breaking down organisational silos.

Historically, we have operated almost like two separate banks: one focused on assets and the other on liabilities. Even within the asset business, certain branches have focused on specific products rather than offering the entire range. We need to move away from this structure and become one integrated bank serving multiple needs of the same customer.

For example, every MSME (micro, small and medium enterprise) customer should ideally have a current account with us; most of our liability customers should be potential credit card customers; loan customers should also be brought into our deposit franchise. These opportunities will allow us to generate additional business from existing customers without significantly increasing operating costs.

Over the next six to twelve months, we want to make substantial progress in breaking down these silos. This will create operating leverage and help improve our CI ratio. Our focus,  therefore, is on profitable growth rather than growth at any cost. We have not indicated a specific numerical target for the CI ratio at this stage.

How far have your plans to transition into a universal bank progressed?

We believe Equitas is already positioned well above most small finance banks in terms of market awareness, brand positioning and operating capabilities. However, we now need to move beyond thinking of ourselves purely as a small finance bank (SFB).

We need to position ourselves as a full-fledged bank, both internally and in the minds of our customers. The obvious next step in this journey is obtaining a universal banking licence. We do intend to apply for the licence.

My personal assessment is that we could apply within calendar year 2027. The regulator expects us to move in this direction, and logically, we are among the next institutions in the small finance banking space to pursue this transition. However, the leadership transition must first be completed, and the permanent CEO will have an important role in taking the application forward.

I believe we are well positioned to qualify on the relevant parameters. Obtaining a universal banking licence would provide several advantages, particularly in terms of cost of funds and capital flexibility.

What are the advantages of transitioning into a universal bank?

The advantage of transitioning into a universal bank would be the ability to move away from the SFB classification. Today, we pay relatively higher interest rates on deposits, partly because of our positioning as a SFB.

Once we become a universal bank, we expect to rationalise our deposit pricing. This will reduce the cost of funds. Even a reduction of about 75 basis points in the cost of funds could have a significant positive impact on our profitability. It would also allow us to serve higher-quality customers on the asset side, including relatively more affluent customer segments with better credit profiles.

So, moving away from the SFB structure would be particularly beneficial for our liabilities franchise and overall profitability.

What new products and services do you plan to introduce?

We intend to introduce new two-wheeler financing. Currently, we offer financing for used two-wheelers, but we want to expand into a more comprehensive two-wheeler financing proposition.

We also see significant potential in the corporate salary segment. At present, our liabilities franchise is largely focused on individual customers. We do not yet have a fully developed corporate banking proposition. Given the attractive savings rates we offer, employees of corporate organisations could be interested in banking with us. We, therefore,  need to build stronger relationships and connectivity with corporates.

Given that Equitas is a South-based bank, where gold financing is traditionally a strong business, why is your gold loan portfolio still small at 2 per cent of your gross advances of Rs 50,669 crore?

We have not performed as well as we could have in this segment, despite having the necessary infrastructure and systems. Last year, we developed a new in-house gold loan system. Following its launch, monthly disbursements increased from approximately ₹20 crore to more than ₹200 crore. We believe the business can grow substantially further.

The key requirements for a successful gold loan business include technology, processes, safe custody arrangements and appropriate valuation mechanisms. We already have all these capabilities in place. Our challenge has primarily been on the distribution and sales side.

We need to improve coordination between our asset and liability branches, re-train our sales teams and strengthen our ability to market gold loans. Given the relatively small existing portfolio, gold loans could become one of our fastest-growing businesses in percentage terms.

data.title: Waaree Transpower bags over ₹100 crore NTPC order for battery storage project
data.description:
Waaree Transpower Pvt Ltd., a subsidiary of Waaree Energies Ltd., has secured an order worth over ₹100 crore from state-run power major NTPC for the supply of inverter duty transformers for its battery energy storage system (BESS) project.

The order involves transformers ranging from 11 MVA to 22 MVA and marks Waaree Transpower’s entry into NTPC’s approved supplier ecosystem for specialised electrical equipment used in grid-scale energy storage projects, stated an official release.

“India’s energy transition is moving beyond the expansion of renewable generation towards building the infrastructure required to store, manage and deliver power reliably. Battery Energy Storage Systems will be central to this next phase, and specialised electrical equipment will play an equally important role in making this transition possible,” stated Viren Doshi, Director, Waaree Energies.

He added that NTPC’s approval and the order represented an important validation of the company’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities, with Waaree looking to strengthen its specialised transformer solutions for energy storage, renewable integration and grid infrastructure.

Waaree Transpower, formerly known as Kotsons, manufactures power and distribution transformers, with a focus on inverter duty transformers for renewable energy applications.

data.title: Investors Lower Expectations of BOE Rate Increase in December — Market Talk
data.description: Markets narrowly cut their expectations of the Bank of England increasing interest rates at the December 17 meeting following this week's U.K. jobs and inflation data releases. The data indicated resilient activity but showed no evidence of high energy prices spreading into broader domestic inflation pressures, MUFG Bank's Henry Cook says in a note. data.title: AI boom, West Asia conflict pushes PCB costs up by almost 40%
data.description:
The global AI infrastructure boom and geopolitical tensions in West Asia are driving up the cost of printed circuit boards (PCBs) by as much as 40 per cent, squeezing Indian electronics manufacturers and threatening to push up prices of consumer electronics.

Richard Puthota, Senior Director at electronics manufacturing firm MacDermid Alpha, said that copper laminates and resin are both important componets to make a PCB, and both have seen a steep rise in cost.

“PCBs today cost almost 40 per cent higher. Additionally, suppliers are prioritising sales to data centre builders and other electronic manufacturers are seeing lead times as long as 12 weeks compared to lower, more consistent timelines in the past,” he added.

A PCB is a board that is used to mechanically support and connect electronic components. China makes the most PCBs in the world, making up around 60 per cent of global production. It is the central nervous system of all electronic products right from a smartphone to TVs to washing machines and more. Industry players peg India’s current PCB demand at around $8 billion worth, with almost 80 per cent imported.

A good thing is that by the end of 2027, we should have at least 2-3 domestic large capacity additions in PCBs and the existing players are also expanding capacity, Puthota notes.

Electronics major Syrma SGS is one such EMS player that is coming up with its own large PCB making plant in Andhra.

“The PCB industry has faced significant cost pressures and supply constraints, led by combination of geopolitical conflict and global supply diversions toward AI and network infrastructure, starving mainstream automotive and industrial sectors,” Jasbir Singh Gujral, MD, Syrma SGS Technology Ltd, said.

The shortage, which emerged in early 2026, is expected to ease around mid-2027, he estimates. Our PCB facility is expected to commence trial production in Q4 FY27, with volume production targeted in FY28, he added.

Rajneesh Garg, President, Indian Printed Circuit Board Association (IPCA), says that due to the shortage of inputs, some of the smaller PCB factories in India are on the verge of closure.

“The cascading effect of this is a steep rise in prices of electronic goods to the extent that sales will be impacted. We are already seeing it happen,” he said.

Garg said the Association is in touch with Government on this issue, and stressed on the need for anti-dumping duty to continue for the industry and also bring in more stringent measures to ensure it’s not being circumvented.

“There are also a few other components of a PCB that are currently not under zero duty, and can be made so,” he recommended.

data.title: GTA VI Sales Top $1.6B — Take-Two, Console Partners Microsoft And Sony Shares Rise
data.description:
Key points:
  • GTA VI is currently available only on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
  • AMD stock also rose after the team behind GTA VI highlighted that it used an AMD system to scale images in the Xbox version's gameplay.
  • Retail sentiment for TTWO shifted to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ as of early Thursday, while the sentiment for MSFT remained ‘bearish.’

Social media platforms X and Reddit were filled on Thursday with praise for Take-Two Interactive’s newly released ‘Grand Theft Auto VI,’ with sales continuing to rise sharply and boosting shares of the gaming giant and console partners Microsoft (MSFT) and Japan’s Sony Corp.

Over 17 million copies of the game were sold worldwide as of Thursday morning, totaling $1.65 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower. TTWO stock rose 1% in premarket trading on Thursday, after an over 6% rally in the previous session.

Microsoft shares rose 1.6%, while Sony stock closed nearly 3% higher in Tokyo on Thursday. ‘GTA VI’ is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch. As of now, the PlayStation version accounted for three-quarters of the overall sales, according to Sensor Tower.

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) also rose 3% in premarket trading after the team behind GTA VI highlighted that it used an AMD system to scale images in the Xbox version's gameplay.

The game drew accolades on social media, with users across X and Reddit calling it “mind-blowing” and “generational.” Fans in particular praised the lifelike visuals, dense world, and little details, while memes showed that some were even taking the day off from work and school to try it out.

Take-Two’s Q2 Recap

Even though GTA VI is a huge draw for Take-Two, the gaming company kept its 2027 booking forecast unchanged ahead of the launch.

On Nov. 9, Take-Two raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to between $7.98 ⁠billion and $8.18 billion, up from $7.90 billion to $8.10 billion earlier. It also raised the lower end of its per-share profit outlook.

In the second quarter, revenue fell to $1.5 billion from $1.77 billion a year ago, missing analyst expectations of $1.62 billion. Total net bookings fell 18% to $1.6 billion.

The current version of the game, ‘GTA V,’ is one of the best-selling games of all time, with over 230 million ‌units ⁠sold since its 2013 launch.

Retail View On TTWO, MSFT

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TTWO shifted to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ as of early Thursday, while the sentiment for MSFT remained ‘bearish.’

“$TTWO this will be the biggest game in the next decade. Trains leaving,” a trader wrote. Another expressed caution, saying “$TTWO wait till the official numbers are released and online launches omg.”

Year to date, TTWO stock is down 15.4%.

data.description: Novartis has sought to address concerns about its ability to replace sales lost due to patent expirations after 2030, but some of its long-term commitments rely on products that face questions, Jefferies analysts say. data.description: Oil prices tick higher as the market weighs expectations of a surplus against continued threats to shipping in the Persian Gulf. In early European trading, Brent crude is up 0.6% to $92.52 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 0.4% to $83.61 a barrel. data.title: DP World raises Mozambique’s Maputo container terminal investment to $200mn, targets 650,000 TEUs by 2027
data.description:
Dubai-based logistics group DP World has raised its planned investment in Mozambique’s Maputo container terminal by $35mn to $200mn, increasing the facility’s annual handling capacity target to 650,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) by the second quarter of 2027 as construction continues on the port expansion.

The revised commitment represents a 21.2% increase from the original $165mn investment, and the new capacity target exceeds the previous one of 530,000 TEUs, DP World announced on November 18.

The company said the expansion would nearly triple annual handling capacity from 225,000 TEUs, although its May 2025 announcement cited a higher starting capacity of 255,000 TEUs.

The announcement followed discussions between DP World group executive chairman Essa Kazim and Mozambican President Daniel Chapo on expanding port operations, strengthening trade infrastructure and improving regional transport connections.

Construction began in May 2025, with the original programme providing for extending the terminal’s quay from 308 metres to 650 metres and deepening its berths from 12 metres to 16 metres, enabling the terminal to handle post-Panamax vessels up to 366 metres long. The programme also raises refrigerated container capacity to 715 plugs from 450.

“Mozambique has an opportunity to become one of Southern Africa’s most important trade gateways,” Kazim said.

DP World operates the Maputo container terminal and is an indirect shareholder in Maputo Port Development Company (MPDC), which holds the port concession until 2058. MPDC is a partnership between Mozambique’s state ports and rail company CFM and Portus Indico, a consortium of DP World, Grindrod and Mozambique Gestores.

South African logistics group Grindrod holds an indirect 24.7% stake in MPDC.

The investment forms part of efforts to strengthen the Maputo Corridor, which links the port with South Africa’s industrial heartland and neighbouring markets.

DP World is also strengthening regional road and rail logistics links, supported by its inland logistics hub at Komatipoort in South Africa.

In a separate announcement on November 2, the company said it would launch a weekly China Africa Link shipping service in late November, connecting Shanghai, Ningbo and Nansha with Dar es Salaam and Maputo via Port Klang in Malaysia.
